situation.roe_position: Frontdoor is a home-warranty and builder-warranty services company, not a bank or insurer. Its return on book equity is extremely high (1.07 in 2025) because buybacks have shrunk the equity base, not because profits are unusual. Treasury stock of $988M offsets retained earnings of $1,068M, leaving equity of $315M against about $283M of nine-month net income. The ratio is a leverage and buyback artefact. Underlying earnings are steady and growing, with 2026 net income likely near $290M. Fourth-quarter earnings are tiny because of seasonality.
situation.why: Nothing in the evidence shows regulatory capital limiting the company. The 2-10 HBW insurance-backed warranty unit does carry some regulatory capital (deferred reinsurance, unearned premium), but it is small against the group. Book equity growth is set by the payout choice: nearly all free cash flow goes to repurchases, with a new $1B authorization. The risk is that equity stays very small or near zero while debt of about $1.15B remains.

The ratio reflects buyback policy as well as profitability. Earnings are real: nine-month 2026 net income was $283 million. Q4 is seasonally tiny, with about 1 percent of 2025 net income.
